hook.line: Walk down any street in La Candelaria and the walls are full of short, firm notices. You will read them every day, and sooner or later you will need to say one yourself.
hook.en: Going in without an appointment is forbidden.

examples.en: Going in without an appointment is forbidden.

examples.es: No se permite entrar con perros.

rule:
Spanish forbids things at three levels.

On signs: *Prohibido el paso*, *No tocar*. Just the bare infinitive.

Official notices: *Está prohibido*, *No está permitido* or *No se permite*, then an infinitive.

Everyday speech: *Aquí no se puede fumar*.

Nothing goes between the phrase and the infinitive: no *de*, no *a*. The English "-ing" ("smoking") becomes an infinitive (*fumar*).

To tell one person off, use a command: *No fumes aquí*.
smallPrint: Teachers call the sign style an infinitive used as a command, and *no se permite* a passive *se*.

options: You may go in without an appointment.
Going in without an appointment is forbidden.
Don't smoke here, please. (to a friend)

readAndPick.es: No se permite entrar con perros.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (Taking photos is not allowed): ___ tomar fotos. (*No está permitido* / *Está permitido*)
Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (You can't smoke here): Aquí ___ fumar. (*no se puede* / *se puede*)
yourTurn.why: You can't smoke is *no se puede*, and the infinitive follows.

yourTurn.prompt: Type the sign in Spanish: No entry.
yourTurn.why: Signs are short: *prohibido* plus what is banned.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Going in without an appointment is forbidden.
yourTurn.why: *Está prohibido* goes straight into the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Dogs are not allowed in.
yourTurn.answer: No se permite entrar con perros.
yourTurn.why: *No se permite* is the notice style for what is not allowed.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell one friend not to smoke here: Aquí no se puede fumar.
yourTurn.why: To one person you use the command *fumes*.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn it into a sign: No se puede tocar.
yourTurn.why: A sign drops everything and keeps *no* plus the infinitive.

pitfalls.wrong: Está prohibido de entrar sin cita.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Nothing goes between *prohibido* and the infinitive, so no *de*.
A ban on a notice is a state of things, so Spanish uses *está*.
To tell one person not to do something, the verb takes the command form *fumes*.

personal: Look around where you are right now. Write one thing that is forbidden or not allowed, with *Está prohibido…* or *No se puede…*.
